title: How many right angled triangles have this long side?
description: The long side of five centimetres is fixed as the base. Since the other two angles must add up to ninety degrees, many choices for one angle give many different triangles. The video tries three choices and then counts.
teaching_notes: One idea: with the long side fixed and the right angle at the top, every choice of one base angle gives a different triangle. Watch for students who think the triangle is fixed once the long side is given.

source: Construct a right-angled triangle ABC with ∠B = 90° and AC = 5 cm. How many different triangles exist with these measurements? [Hint: Note that the other measurements can take any values. Take AC as the base. What values can ∠A and ∠C take so that the other angle is 90°?]
video_script.why: The child can name a right angled triangle and use the angle sum, and now sees that one side and one right angle do not fix the triangle.
video_script.substitution: Fix AC = 5 cm as the base, find that the two base angles add up to 90°, and try three choices for ∠A.
video_script.anchor: a base AC of five centimetres with a right angle at B above it
video_script.payoff_line: There are infinitely many such triangles

final_answer.value: Infinitely many: ∠A can be any value strictly between 0° and 90° with ∠C = 90° - ∠A
final_answer.spoken: there are infinitely many such triangles

maths_rules: choose ∠A = 30°, then ∠C = 90° - 30° = 60°; choose ∠A = 45°, then ∠C = 45°; choose ∠A = 70°, then ∠C = 90° - 70° = 20°
each choice gives arms that cross at a different place B, so a different triangle
∠A can be any value strictly between 0° and 90°, and ∠C = 90° - ∠A, so there are infinitely many triangles
video_script.design: The base AC stays fixed on the board. Two arms leave A and C at chosen angles and cross at B; three choices are drawn one after the other, and the crossing point B moves.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many different triangles eigh bee cee we can make.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, the three angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees. The angle at bee is ninety.
<bookmark mark='take'/>One hundred and eighty take away ninety is ninety.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Together, the angles at eigh and cee make ninety degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='thirty'/>Step two, choose thirty degrees at eigh. Then the angle at cee is ninety take away thirty, which is sixty. The arms cross at bee.
<bookmark mark='fortyfive'/>Choose forty five degrees at eigh. Then the angle at cee is also forty five, and the arms cross at a new bee.

<bookmark mark='three'/>The three positions of bee are different, so the three triangles are different.

narration: <bookmark mark='range'/>Step four, the angle at eigh can be any value between zero and ninety degrees. It cannot be zero or ninety.
<bookmark mark='partner'/>The angle at cee is then ninety take away the angle at eigh.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are infinitely many such triangles.
<bookmark mark='why'/>We can choose from too many values for the angle at eigh to count them.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check, thirty plus ninety plus sixty is one hundred and eighty.
